tagline: Up the Logan River and over the top to turquoise water.
intro: From Logan, US 89 goes up the canyon beside the Logan River, between deeply cut limestone walls laden with fossils and some 500 million years of geologic history. It climbs about 2,900 feet to a summit near 7,800. Just over the top the overlooks take in Bear Lake, and then the road drops steeply to Garden City on its shore.

Thomas Ricks and his neighbors began the road at Brigham Young's suggestion, and within a decade the stretch to Ricks Spring was a favorite outing for camping and automobiling. In 1903 Horatio Nelson Jackson stopped in Garden City on the first automobile trip across the country.

moments.title: Jardine Juniper
moments.text: A Rocky Mountain juniper long credited with 3,000 years. Cores taken in the 1950s put it nearer 1,500, which is still a long while to stand in one canyon.

moments.title: Ricks Spring
moments.text: Visitors carried home barrels of its spring water and came down with giardia. In 1972 dye put into the Logan River turned up here, coming back out of the limestone.

moments.title: Bear Lake
moments.text: From the overlooks just past the summit the lake shows the turquoise that suspended calcium carbonate gives it, the color behind its name, the Caribbean of the Rockies.

practical: The canyon road is winding with sharp changes in elevation, and winter weather makes it hazardous.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Logan Canyon National Scenic Byway
